nodes.title: Behavioral Guidelines and Project Rules
nodes.summary: Core project documentation defining coding standards, architectural constraints, and a Turkish-English naming convention.
nodes.description: This document serves as the primary technical and behavioral guide for the LevelTodo project. It outlines four general principles: thinking before coding, simplicity, surgical changes, and goal-driven execution. Specifically for LevelTodo, it mandates that Domain and Application layers remain pure Python (no PyQt6 dependencies), enforces the use of a central clock interface (IClock), and establishes a naming convention where domain logic uses Turkish terms (ASCII-safe) while technical infrastructure uses standard English software terms.
nodes.languageNotes: The project uses a hybrid naming strategy: Turkish for domain concepts (e.g., 'gorev' for task) and English for architectural patterns (e.g., 'repository', 'service').
nodes.languageLesson: Using native language for domain logic helps align code with business requirements, while keeping infrastructure terms in English ensures compatibility with standard libraries and developer expectations.

nodes.title: Alembic Migration Configuration
nodes.summary: Configuration file for database schema migrations using Alembic.
nodes.description: Defines the environment for Alembic migrations. It specifies the location of migration scripts within the infrastructure layer and configures logging for the migration process. Note that the database URL is intentionally left empty as it is injected programmatically at runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Configures how SQL changes are tracked and applied.
nodes.languageLesson: Decoupling migration configuration from the specific database URL allows for more flexible environment-based deployments.

nodes.title: Python Project Configuration
nodes.summary: Central metadata and dependency management for the Python project.
nodes.description: A standard PEP 518 configuration file that manages build requirements, project metadata, and dependencies (including PyQt6, SQLAlchemy, and Alembic). it also configures development tools like Ruff for linting and Pytest for testing, and defines the 'leveltodo' CLI entry point.
nodes.languageNotes: Lists all external libraries required to run and develop the application.
nodes.languageLesson: The pyproject.toml file is the modern standard for Python project configuration, replacing older files like setup.py and requirements.txt.
